verdict.rationale: a-Shell ships its own Apple Shortcuts actions, such as `Execute Command` and `Put File`/`Get File`, which let users script multi-step file-processing workflows. Shortcuts can also be forced to run "in Extension" rather than in the app, though the docs warn this won't always work. Autonomous triggering and scheduling come from the host Shortcuts platform rather than from a-Shell itself, and a-Shell documents no native background scheduler, so this is only partial support. Missing for 10: native scheduled or triggered background execution (cron-like), documented reliability of unattended runs, agentic/AI-driven automation, independent hands-on corroboration.
